Welcome
A very warm welcome to our school website. Dinglewell Infant School is a large Infant School with 270 pupils aged between 4 and 7 years old and is located on the outskirts of Gloucester, in Hucclecote.
Our school is open Monday to Friday, with the school day running from 8:45am until 3:15pm.
Classroom doors open at 8:40am and close at 8:45am. Children should arrive during this five-minute window to ensure they are settled and ready for the start of the school day. If your child is late, please bring them to the school office where you will be asked to sign your child in to our late register.
We look forward to welcoming your child each day.
We aim to treat every child as an individual and provide a secure, safe, happy, welcoming and thriving environment. We offer exciting learning experiences which have creativity at the heart.
This website aims to give you a taster of the school, as well as providing up to date information for parents, pupils and the wider community. We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find the information you are looking for; please contact the school office with any queries you may have, or parents may request paper copies of information free of charge.
Our Y1 & Y2 parents recently completed a survey which I would like to share with you before you look any further into the life of Dinglewell Infant School.
"Dinglewell is a fantastic school! It makes its pupils feel safe, valued & they enjoy coming. My daughter has flourished being at Dinglewell. The staff are lovely & nothing is too much trouble! Can't wait for my son to start!"
"The school has a lovely atmosphere & teachers who care."
"A lovely balance of nurturing & learning through fun activities. My child's progress has been significant at each stage of his development."
"The school feels like a family environment where each child is nurtured academically, socially & emotionally."
Together we Develop, Inspire, Succeed
Our vision as a school community is to:
Develop self-esteem, respect and a sense of personal achievement
Inspire a love of learning and a commitment to others
Succeed in achieving our vision within a safe, healthy, creative and stimulating environment
We recognise that the impact of our values is not in what we say, but in the experiences to which we expose our children.
"The values of the school are reflected in the sense of purpose, the caring, the high standard and the drive and commitment." (Ofsted Report Nov 2013)
We value ourselves, other people, their views, and the environment
We are independent and make good decisions for ourselves and others
We think for ourselves and enjoy exploring different ways of doing things
We are friendly and work together
We look after other people and keep ourselves safe
We tell the truth and can be trusted
At Dinglewell Infant School we aim:
To value ‘play’ as fundamental to learning

Maths at Home
Maths at Home
July 2026​ - An old favourite: Shut the Box​
This classic board game supports the recall on number bonds and rapid calculation. It also promotes problem solving and strategic thinking.​
You can play as a family and just need two 1-6 dice and a strip of numbers from 1 through to 9.​
The goal is for each player to cover up (or cross out) as many numbers as possible on their game board and have the lowest score remaining at the end of the game. ​
The Rules: Decide what order the players are going to go in. This could be based on youngest to oldest or you could each roll the dice and the largest number rolled is the first player. Player One will roll both dice and add the numbers together to find the total. They then need to create a calculation that adds up to that total. Once they have done this, they record the numbers used in their calculation on their game board (by covering them with counters or crossing them out with a pencil). They cannot use these numbers in any other calculations so need to think very carefully about which ones they choose! For example if Player One rolls a five and a two, their total is seven. They can decide which numbers they want to use on their game board to add together to make seven. It could be five and two like they have rolled or it could be any other calculation that makes seven. It does not have to be just two numbers added together either. It could be one, two and four or just the number seven by itself. Once Player One has rolled their dice, added them together and then covered up (or crossed out) the numbers they have used, it is Player Two’s turn. They roll the dice and do the same thing. Each player keeps taking turns until they cannot use their remaining numbers to make the total on the dice. They add up the numbers that they have left and that is their final score. The lowest final score decides the winner of the game. If a player manages to use all of their numbers up, they automatically win.​
Please email photos of your family enjoying this game to Mrs Bishop ​
ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk​
and I will share them on the school website. Please visit the website to see the photos of Pattern Professors that were sent to me last month. ​
June 2026 - Pattern Professors
This month's activity is to create a repeated pattern. Be as creative as you like. ​
​Please email your patterns to Mrs Bishop ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk so that they can be shared on the ​school website.
May 2026 - Sizzling Symmetry
Design a symmetrical image. This could be a photograph or a piece of patterned artwork.​
Well done to Freddie and Theo who sent these amazing examples of symmetry:
April 2026 - Maths Games
I have fond memories of playing a game of Ludo with my family when I was a child. Does your family have a favourite game that promotes maths skills. Now as an adult Mr Bishop and I enjoy playing the card game Crazy Eights. ​
This month I would love to see pictures of our Dinglewell families playing their favourite maths game; please let me know the rules of the game as it may be a new one that I can incorporate at school. Class 5 are very familiar with Snakes and Ladders and this can be played with two dice to promote addition skills. ​
Please email your maths games photos and rules to Mrs Bishop ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk and I will share them on the ​
Our Book Worms
Spinderella doesn't have a clue about numbers and her Hairy Godmother teaches her all abou
Franky tell us that "Spinderella doesn’t have a clue about numbers and her Hairy Godmother teaches her all about them!"
March 2026 - Book Worms
Can you find maths in a book? To link with World Book Day, I have chosen a book-based activity for next month. While you’re reading look out for any maths links? There may be maths in an old favourite story, a school reading book, a non-fiction book or even in poem. ​
Ask a grown up to take a photo of you reading your book, so that I can see the front cover and tell me all about the maths that you have spotted within the book. ​
​Please email your book worm photos and quotes to Mrs Bishop ​
ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk​
and I will share them on the school website.
Look at the amazing Foodie Maths that has been found at home last month.
February 2026 - Foodie Maths
Can you find maths disguised as food?​
Please take a photo, write down or draw what you have spotted. Here are 2 simple ideas to get you started.​
3 sets of 2 cupcakes​
2 and 2 and 2 make 6 cupcakes altogether.​
​Please email your foodie maths pictures to Mrs Bishop ​
ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk​
and I will share them on the school website. ​
December 2025 - Rudolph Maths
Create an image of Rudolph the Red Nosed Reindeer using 2D shapes. Please remember to label the shapes that you have used. Here are a couple of ideas to get you started. Please email a photo of your 2D shape Rudolph to
ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk
This reindeer was created by a former pupil and he still make me smile.
November 2025 - NumBots
This month's activity focuses on our on-line learning platform NumBots. NumBots is an excellent way to support your child’s maths learning at school and their developing number sense. ​
Mrs Bishop will monitor usage during November and the class that has the highest percentage of children playing will be awarded our robot mascot for the month. Play can then continue each month with the mascot awarded to the class sustaining their efforts at home. If you need a copy of your child’s login details, please email Mrs Bishop ​
ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk
We are delighted to announce that Class 3 are the winners with 67% of the class engaging with maths learning at home. Well done.
Mrs Bishop will continue to monitor play each month and continue to award the mascot. Please check the news letter for each month's winner.​
October 2025 - 4 Dominoes Challenge
Use these four dominoes to make a square that has the same number of dots on each side.​
​What did you do to try to solve this challenge? ​
Use this QR code to access a printable version of the problem ​
Please email your solutions to Mrs Bishop ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk​
September 2025 - En-Counters for Two
Arranging counters activity for adult and child. ​
Can you create the pattern of counters that your partner ​
has made, just by asking questions? ​
Here's a game to play with an adult!​
You'll need an adult to play with.​ You also need two matching sets of counters (or something similar - bottle tops, coloured circles of paper etc) - up to 12 in each set. ​ Give one set to the adult and keep the other set for yourself. ​ Make a secret place where the adult can hide the counters. You could make a screen with a book, or do it on a tray and cover it up with a piece of cloth.​ The adult secretly makes a pattern or design with some of the counters, describing what they are doing as they make it.​ Your job is to make the same design by asking questions, which the adult answers as helpfully as possible.​ When you think you have a completed design, ask the adult to check.​ If you're right you could swap roles.​ If you're wrong keep going!​ How many questions did you need to ask?​
Top tip: it may be helpful to start with a simple pattern such as a straight line with just 3 or 4 counters and build up the complexity from there.​
Mrs Bishop would love to see photos of you playing this game so please send photos to ebishop@dinglewell-inf.gloucs.sch.uk and she will add them to the school website to celebrate maths at home.
Useful Websites

Maths Passport
At Dinglewell Infant School we use Maths Intergalactic Space Travel Passports to support the development of rapid recall of key mathematical facts. The children travel around the solar system progressing from planet to planet. Each planet has 4 main objectives. Rapid recall is developed by practice and repetition and your support at home is key to this.
We ask parents to help at home and help guides are available for each planet. The help guides contain ideas on questioning and some useful websites. Please find time to play maths games, practise counting patterns and ask questions on a weekly basis. The children love their passports and are keen to show off their skills and consequently move on to a new planet. There are many good maths websites available and new ones appear from time to time, so if you find one that is really good please let Mrs Bishop know so that she can pass the information on to other parents.
Please remember to revisit objectives from previous passports as it is really important that they can still be recalled rapidly whenever needed.

Reading at Home
Read, read, read! This is the most crucial, valuable and rewarding thing that you can do to support your child with their learning. In terms of reading scheme books, Oxford Owl is a good free online resource (which supports our school reading scheme), with a wide range of ebooks available for your child to read. You will be able to select books dependent on their age and reading ability.
It is absolutely fine for children to re-read books, in fact this helps children in the early stages of reading to become more fluent and increase their confidence.

Curriculum
At Dinglewell Infant School our carefully-crafted curriculum is rooted in our school vision 'Together we Develop, Inspire, Succeed' and it is from this that our aims come:
Our approach follows the National Curriculum (2014) and complies with our duties set out in the Equality Act 2010 and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014; making our curriculum accessible for those with disabilities or special educational needs. We follow a topic-based approach which is carefully planned and crafted by our staff to make learning inspiring, experiential, thought provoking, and fun.
At the heart of all we do at Dinglewell we have six core values that drive our curriculum:
As a staff we strive to nourish imaginations and nurture creative expression. To us, creativity means more than the arts alone; for us it is a way of thinking and an approach to life.
Our pupils learn to develop adaptable, flexible and critical thinking and to express their own thoughts, feelings and ideas. Whether that's crafting a painting, explaining their reasoning, or resolving a conflict - we actively develop children's ability to confidently express themselves in a variety of ways and in an environment where they are encouraged to be themselves, take risks, and should they fail, try again.
All learning is built on previous knowledge and pupils have a wealth of opportunities to develop links between topics and subjects. Progressive key vocabulary is woven into all subject areas and topics, to ensure that it is 'taught' not 'caught', and explicitly underpins the children's learning. Our topics are chosen to build a rich bank of knowledge and foster a love for learning.
Every term class teachers in each year group provide a detailed outline of the topics and focus to be covered in each subject.
Please see Curriculum Overviews for Parents section below.

Curriculum
Parent Information Meetings were held in classrooms, after school, in July for each Year 1 and Year 2 with an EYFS information meeting in September, to help you to understand our approach to learning in your child's new class. For those that were unable to attend the meetings, the teachers have put together a short slide show with the intention of helping you to understand our approach at school, and also how best you can support your child/ren at home. The slides are less detailed than the presentations themselves, but do give an overview. Please ask your child's class teacher if there is anything you're unsure about.
Curriculum Overviews for parents/carers can also be found on the website at the beginning of each term or new topic (see above).
These give an overview of what will be taught in every subject over a specific amount of time.
Year 1 and 2 overviews also offer a choice of home projects for you to support your child/ren with at home if you choose - these are very popular with the children and can be completed in a way that best suits your family.
